_why: Two different things live in this file, and conflating them would break the gate.
`documented` is a list of GATE RULES. Each one excuses a RENDERED element that
computes off the type ramp. computed-type-check.mjs consults these, and a rule
that matches nothing is a FAILURE, not a harmless leftover — see `_deadRules`
below. Only add an entry here when a real element really does compute off-ramp.
`figmaUnbindable` is a RECORD, not a rule. It documents every text node in the
Figma file that cannot be bound to a ramp step, whether or not code renders it
off-ramp. Nothing in it affects the gate. It exists because the ramp question
was decided Option B on 10 Aug 2026 — keep the 14-step ramp, bind the nodes to
it — and these 31 nodes are the residue that decision leaves behind.
WHY THE TWO LISTS ARE DIFFERENT LENGTHS
31 Figma nodes cannot be bound. Only 8 rendered elements actually compute
off-ramp, because for most of the 31 the code already snapped to a ramp step
(a code/Figma divergence, recorded per entry) or renders no text at all. Adding
a gate rule for those would create a rule matching nothing, which is worse than
useless: it would sit dormant until some unrelated element happened to match its
triple, and then silently excuse a real regression.
HOW A `documented` ENTRY IS KEYED, AND WHY IT CANNOT HIDE A DELETION
Each entry requires BOTH an exact computed triple AND the continued presence of
every class in `requireClasses`. tailwind-merge deleting a ramp class removes it
from the DOM, so `requireClasses` stops matching, the exception stops applying,
and the element fails like any other. An exception can only ever excuse the exact
composition it names.
NOT IN THIS FILE, and deliberately so: <option>/<optgroup> (drawn by the platform
inside the native select popup, where Chrome forces line-height:normal), anything
inside .sr-only (clipped to 1px, never seen), and classless text (which merely
inherits). Those are structural exclusions in computed-type-check.mjs, reported
as warnings rather than silently dropped.
_deadRules: A `documented` entry that matches zero rendered elements fails the gate.
This is deliberate and it is the whole reason this file can be trusted over time.
An exception is a standing permission to be wrong in one exact way; once the
thing it was excusing is gone, the permission has to go too. Without this check
the file would accumulate stale rules, and a stale rule is a loaded gun pointed
at some future element that happens to compute the same triple.
If the gate reports a dead rule, delete the entry — do not soften it.

documented.reason: The ramp has no 11px semibold step — Label/XS is 11/16 MEDIUM — so the component takes the nearest step and overrides the weight. Size matches the file, leading is 2px looser, weight matches by override rather than by binding. Medium and large initials WERE bound on 10 Aug 2026 (Heading/XS, Heading/LG); small is the one that could not be.

The ramp has no 12px semibold step. Body/XS is 12/18 REGULAR, so size and leading match the file exactly and only the weight is an override — the closest any of these three get to the file. Snapping to Label/SM instead would have matched the weight and broken the leading.

The check glyph inside the 16px box. Marked ASSERTED in source: no box tokens are recorded anywhere for this component, and the ramp has no 10px step at all. The repo rule is to flag rather than invent a token, so the raw value stands and is flagged here. Note code renders 10px where the file draws 12px — this is the one entry where code and Figma disagree on SIZE, not just leading.

figmaUnbindable._decision: Option B, 10 Aug 2026 — the 14-step ramp stays as it is. See docs/design-system/decisions/2026-08-10-figma-side-decision-memo.md item 1, and the ramp-additions proposal at 2026-08-10-ramp-additions-proposal.md for what it would take to retire these.
